title: Paradoxes of Infinity as Reductio ad Absurdum

rows.label: A1
rows.predicate: The classical theorems, accepted unchanged: G\"odel~I and Rosser, Tarski's undefinability, Turing's halting theorem, Cantor's theorem and uncountability, Russell, Burali--Forti, Skolem, Vitali, Hausdorff, Banach--Tarski; the operational paradoxes (Hilbert's hotel, Zeno). No classical derivation is disputed.

rows.label: A2
rows.predicate: Metamathematics: Robinson's $Q$, essentially undecidable, every model infinite; $\mathrm{Con}(Q)$ by cut elimination in $I\Delta_0+\mathrm{superexp}$, not in $I\Delta_0+\mathrm{exp}$; Tait's finitism; Dedekind's categoricity of the second-order naturals; true second-order arithmetic not arithmetical; Tarski's decidable real field; Solovay's model and Shelah's inaccessible.

rows.label: A3
rows.predicate: Combinatorics and set theory: Fraenkel--Mostowski permutation models (symmetry as an obstruction to choice); de~Bruijn--Erd\H{o}s compactness of colouring; aperiodic tile sets and the undecidability of the domino problem (Berger, Robinson); Zermelo's choice.

rows.label: A4
rows.predicate: The corpus: the totality finite and complete (00:A4), counting closes by return (00:A7), a bounded observer a proper part and every reading a projection (00:A5, A6), G\"odel vacuous over the finite $\Omega$ (00:Z1), the $\Omega$-hard demarcation (00:Z3); finite mathematics as ontologically primary (Lev, Zeilberger).

rows.label: B1
rows.predicate: The standing hypotheses: (Eff) effective axiomatisation, (Arith) interpretability of $Q$, (Cns) consistency. Two doors for infinity: the meta-level syntax, potential and retained; and (IR), the object theory interprets $Q$ --- an injective non-cyclic successor with sequence coding, the completed registry inside the theory.

rows.label: B2
rows.predicate: The bundle $\{$Eff, Cns, Cmp, IR$\}$ is inconsistent, with no soundness assumption: under Eff and IR the Rosser sentence is available, and Cmp decides it against plain consistency.

rows.label: B3
rows.predicate:
Witnessed independence: every three-element subset is satisfiable --- $Q$ itself ($
eg$Cmp, consistent by finitary means, the superexponential cost exact); $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$ ($
eg$IR: consistent, complete, decidable, singly axiomatised, interpreting no $Q$ since every model of $Q$ is infinite); the inconsistent extension ($
eg$Cns); true arithmetic ($
eg$Eff). Four legs, all load-bearing.

rows.label: B4
rows.predicate: The arithmetic frame $W_N$: domain $[0,N)$, constant $0$, order $<$, the graphs $S$, $A$, $M$ of successor, sum and product restricted to the domain (overflow fails the atom); frame truth is truth in $W_N$; a $\Delta_0$ sentence is transcribed through the graphs with guarded bounded quantifiers.

rows.label: B5
rows.predicate: Per-frame completeness: $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$ is consistent, complete and decidable, axiomatised by the categorical sentence $\sigma_N$; truth in any finite structure is decided by evaluation, and the theory of any structure is complete.

rows.label: B6
rows.predicate: Bounded stability, schema form: a $\Delta_0$ sentence $\varphi$ with bound $t(\varphi)$ has $W_N\models\varphi^{*}\iff\N\models\varphi$ for every $N>t(\varphi)$, each instance $\mathrm{St}(\varphi,M)$ a finite conjunction of finite checks; proved for an explicit $\Delta_0$ language with $t(\varphi)$ computed; Goldbach below $20$ has $t=400$ and value true (below $10$, $t=100$, decided by the kernel).

rows.label: B7
rows.predicate: The unbounded quantifier is the internalised registry: a $\Pi^{0}_{1}$ sentence receives a verdict from each frame about its own domain and none about all frames at once; frame-relative completeness covers every executed verification (a bounded $\Delta_0$ trace) and no $\Pi^{0}_{1}$ closure.

rows.label: C1
rows.predicate: The bounded agent of capacity $K$: records of at most $K$ symbols over $s\ge2$ letters, fewer than $s^{K+1}$ of them; certification is a retained record encoding a completed proof-check, one sentence per record, no schema compression.

rows.label: C2
rows.predicate: No internal mirror: fewer than $s^{K+1}$ records exist, so an agent with $s^{K+1}<N$ holds no injective representation of the domain of $W_N$ --- a proper part cannot mirror the whole (pigeonhole).

rows.label: C3
rows.predicate: Vanishing certified fraction: at least $c^{L}$ normal-form sentences of length $\le L$, half of each cohort frame truths by completeness, fewer than $s^{K+1}$ certified, so the certified fraction is at most $s^{K+1}/\lfloor c^{L}/2\rfloor\to0$.

rows.label: C4
rows.predicate: The migration: without IR every sentence about the totality is decided and incompleteness reappears as a resource bound on agents --- the G\"odel sentence's role passes to truths whose shortest certificate exceeds the capacity; truth for $W_N$ is definable one level up (Tarski relativised to a resource hierarchy).

rows.label: C5
rows.predicate: Horizon separation: halting for machines of bounded space $K$ is decided from above within $|Q|\,K\,s^{K}$ steps (a configuration repeats) and never from within (diagonalisation); Turing's theorem is an external non-existence theorem, classified with Cantor's, not an instance of the bundle.

blocks.title: The reductio principle and the forced selection

rows.label: D1
rows.predicate: The premises and baselines: AT (an absolute totality), IR (the internalised registry), AC$\infty$ (unrestricted choice over uncountable families); Cns, Cmp, Meas (the exact measure axioms of each geometry), and Det --- a totality decides every well-posed question about itself, elements, subsets and relations, with its full second-order theory effectively presented; declared as an axiom.

rows.label: D2
rows.predicate: Antinomy normal form: Cns $+$ AT $+$ comprehension is inconsistent (Russell, Burali--Forti); the witness of Cns $+\neg$AT is bounded comprehension --- every set $u$ has a subset not among its members and no universal set exists, decided on $V_4$.

rows.label: D3
rows.predicate: Diagonal normal form: $\{$Eff, Cns, Cmp, IR$\}$ inconsistent (B2), Tarski a variant with the truth predicate for Cmp; the diagonal is a theorem when external --- Cantor's theorem, $n<2^{n}$ on every frame, uncountability, halting --- and a paradox engine only over an internalised registry with completeness demanded.

rows.label: D4
rows.predicate: Choice normal forms: Vitali (countably additive translation-invariant measure on all subsets $+$ AC$\infty$ on $\R/\Q$, a countable amenable group) and Banach--Tarski (finitely additive isometry-invariant measure $+$ AC$\infty$ $+$ a free non-amenable rotation subgroup) are inconsistent bundles with distinct mechanisms; the finite witness is counting measure with definable choice.

rows.label: D5
rows.predicate: The reductio principle: for each normal form a baseline $B$ and one infinitary premise $I$ with $B+I$ contradictory and $B+\neg I$ satisfiable by an explicit witness --- bounded ranks, $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$, counting measure (Solovay's model as classical corroboration); the rejection of $I$ is coherent and witnessed.

rows.label: D6
rows.predicate: The selection thesis: every normal form conjoins completed infinity with a totalising operation (comprehension, completeness, total selection, a total measure); each is harmless alone, contradiction tracks the conjunction; classical mathematics rejected the totalising conjunct at each crisis, this paper the shared one, the selection settled by Det rather than convention.

rows.label: D7
rows.predicate: Forced exit: Det supplies Eff and Cmp, so $\{$Cns, Det, IR$\}$ is inconsistent and, Cns and Det being constitutive, the reductio is forced against IR --- no determinate totality internalises an unbounded registry; the four-clause bundle condenses to this triad. Conditional on Det.

rows.label: D8
rows.predicate: Finiteness of determinate totalities: in ZF with every infinite set Dedekind-infinite, a structure satisfies Det iff it is finite --- finite: the full higher-order theory decided by exhaustive evaluation; infinite: a copy of $\N$ inside gives an effective reduction of true second-order arithmetic, which is not arithmetical. The real field's first-order tameness is silence about its subsets.

rows.label: D9
rows.predicate: Corollaries: no absolute totality is determinate (a universal set is infinite by the iterated singletons); Meas is decided content --- a Det totality decides every measure question, trivially on a finite one (counting measure). The totalising conjuncts of two normal forms follow from D8.

rows.label: D10
rows.predicate: The three gates: syntactic infinity (meta-level, potential, retained), semantic infinity (a completed object of the theory, the target in all three forms), diagonalisation (a method, dangerous only downstream of the second gate); the paper argues with an unbounded supply of finite objects only.

rows.label: E1
rows.predicate: Global choice on a finite universe: with a canonical order, $\operatorname{ch}(A)=\min A$ is a uniform pointwise choice rule; over a fixed finite base AC is a definable theorem; finite products are nonempty without it.

rows.label: E2
rows.predicate: Periodic choice: an equality-periodic family $A_{i+N}=A_i$ has the choice $f(i)=\operatorname{ch}(A_i)$ of the same period; group-periodic families as equivariant surjections $\pi:A\to I$ with equivariant sections.

rows.label: E3
rows.predicate: Equivariant periodic choice: a $G$-equivariant section exists iff each stabiliser action $G_i\curvearrowright A_i$ has a fixed point (one orbit at a time); the Fraenkel--Mostowski mechanism in positive form.

rows.label: E4
rows.predicate: The definable basis: every subspace of a finite vector space has the greedy $\min$-basis, one definable function on all subspaces; the equivariant obstruction --- $\Z/2$ acting by $v\mapsto-v$ on the line over $\F_5$ fixes no basis ($-v\neq v$), over $\F_2$ it does: arithmetic, not formal.

rows.label: E5
rows.predicate: Periodic K\H{o}nig: in a finite digraph with out-degree $\ge1$ the greedy walk repeats a vertex within $|D|+1$ steps and is eventually periodic with period $\le|D|$ --- the pigeonhole on an iteration over finitely many states.

rows.label: E6
rows.predicate: Periodic de~Bruijn--Erd\H{o}s, dimension one: a $\sigma$-periodic graph of bounded range whose finite subgraphs are $c$-colourable admits a definable $\sigma^{m}$-periodic $c$-colouring (the transfer digraph $D_c$, its sub-digraph of vertices beginning walks of every length, E5).

rows.label: E7
rows.predicate: The dimension boundary: in $\Z^{2}$ aperiodic tile sets exist --- every finite patch admissible, no periodic configuration --- and the domino problem is undecidable; the passage from finite admissibility to infinite realisability has no finite certificate, its demarcation none either. The finite reading asserts patch admissibility only.

rows.label: E8
rows.predicate: The choice paradoxes vanish: on a finite set counting measure is complete and invariant, no decomposition doubles the set ($X\sqcup X$ does not inject into $X$), and every ultrafilter is principal; periodic variants inherit this on one period.

rows.label: F1
rows.predicate: Ontology and conservativeness: actual infinity is an idealisation of the finite; the bounded fragment is kept exactly, the unbounded fragment in schema form; analysis as approximation over finite grids; choice in the small. Positioning: finitism, intuitionism, ultrafinitism, structuralism; the potential-infinity rule retained at the meta-level as a commitment, not a neutrality.

rows.label: F2
rows.predicate: The Reductio Rule and its two tribunals: the economic ledger (the classical exit keeps $\Pi_1$, $\Pi_2$ number theory at a superexponential consistency grant; the finite exit keeps the bounded fragment and declines one classically provable existence claim, E7) and the constitutive Det, on which the verdict rests; objections O1--O5 answered.

rows.label: F3
rows.predicate: The catalogue: the pathologies of the completed infinite in four classes --- antinomies, consistent-but-unregistrable, underdetermination, physical divergences --- each removed by finiteness; the one exclusion retained, the schema over finite instances and the successor act.

rows.label: V1
rows.predicate: The package \texttt{src/5-reductio} (\texttt{finite-ring-space}; $17$ checks, exact, standard library only): \src{a\_frames} A1--A5 (frame theories, no finite model of $Q$, stability with the worked instance and a random sample, the migration counts, the horizon), \src{b\_paradox} B1--B4 ($V_4$, the diagonal, the choice paradoxes, the singletons), \src{c\_choice} C1--C6, \src{d\_determinacy} D1--D2.

rows.label: V2
rows.predicate: \texttt{lean/FrcLedger/Reductio.lean} (Mathlib; classical, tier~2): completeness and decidability of finite structures' theories, models of $Q$ infinite, Cantor, the migration counts and limit, choice and the equivariant criterion, the paradoxes' finite disappearance. \texttt{lean/FrcCore/Reductio.lean} (no axioms, tier~0): the stability schema for an explicit $\Delta_0$ language with its worked instance, the mirror, periodic K\H{o}nig, bounded halting, least-element choice.

rows.label: T1
rows.predicate: The standing of the iteration rule --- whether the potential-infinity rule of the meta-level can be rejected, and at what cost --- is the subject of companion work; the present results are stated to survive either outcome.

B3.name: FRC.Reductio.infinite_of_succ
B3.doc: 5:B3 (Theorem witnessed, exit 2 — `Th(W_N)` does not interpret `Q`): a structure with an injective successor that never reaches zero is infinite; every model of `Q` is such a structure, and a finite frame's definable quotients are finite.

B3.name: FRC.Reductio.theory_complete
B3.doc: 5:B5, 5:B3 (Proposition frame-complete, completeness): the theory of any structure — a finite frame `W_N` among them — is complete: every sentence or its negation is in it.

B5.name: FRC.Reductio.theory_complete
B5.doc: 5:B5, 5:B3 (Proposition frame-complete, completeness): the theory of any structure — a finite frame `W_N` among them — is complete: every sentence or its negation is in it.

B5.name: FRC.Reductio.decRealize
B5.doc: 5:B5 (decidability): in a finite structure with decidable relations, the truth of every bounded formula is decided by evaluation — the quantifiers range over the finitely many elements.

B5.name: FRC.Reductio.decTheory
B5.doc: 5:B5 (Proposition frame-complete, decidability): membership in the theory of a finite structure is decided by evaluating the sentence.

B6.name: FRC.Reductio.stable
B6.doc: 5:B6 (Theorem stability, schema form) — every `Δ₀` formula takes its standard value in every frame `W_N` with `N > t(φ)`: `W_N ⊨ φ* ⟺ ℕ ⊨ φ`, for every environment, by induction on the formula.

B6.name: FRC.Reductio.evalT_frame
B6.doc: 5:B6 (terms) — below its bound a term is defined in the frame, with its standard value.

B6.name: FRC.Reductio.goldbach_ten_stable
B6.doc: 5:B6 — the schema instance `St(goldbach 10, M)` for every `M`: all frames `100 < N` agree with `ℕ`.

C2.name: FRC.Reductio.records_lt
C2.doc: 5:C2 (Proposition mirror, the count): fewer than `s^(K+1)` strings of length at most `K` exist over an alphabet of `s ≥ 2` letters.

C2.name: FRC.Reductio.no_mirror
C2.doc: 5:C2 (Proposition mirror): a part with fewer distinguishable records than the frame has elements admits no injective representation of the frame's domain.

C2.name: FRC.Reductio.records_lt
C2.doc: 5:C2 (the count) — fewer than `s^(K+1)` records exist for an alphabet of `s ≥ 2` letters.

C2.name: FRC.Reductio.no_mirror
C2.doc: 5:C2 (Proposition mirror) — a part with fewer records than the frame has elements holds no injective representation of the frame's domain: no `f : [0, N) → [0, R)` is injective when `R < N`.

C3.name: FRC.Reductio.certified_fraction_tendsto
C3.doc: 5:C3 (Proposition fraction): the certified fraction `s^(K+1) / ⌊c^L/2⌋` of a bounded agent tends to zero as the cohort length `L` grows, for any capacity and any `c > 1`.

C5.name: FRC.Reductio.repeat_below
C5.doc: 5:E5, 5:C5 (Lemma periodic König, the pigeonhole) — on `n` states the iteration from `x` revisits a state within `n` steps: some `i < j ≤ n` have `f^i x = f^j x`.

C5.name: FRC.Reductio.halts_iff_halts_below
C5.doc: 5:C5 (horizon separation) — a run on `n` states reaches a state `h` iff it reaches it within `n` steps: halting for bounded space is decided from above by `n` steps of simulation.

D3.name: FRC.Reductio.cantor
D3.doc: 5:D3 (Remark cantor-diagonal): Cantor's theorem is an external diagonal — no map from a set onto its power set, in every finite frame as `n < 2^n`.

D3.name: FRC.Reductio.cantor_finite
D3.doc: 5:D3 (Remark, the external diagonal) — Cantor's theorem holds in every finite frame: `n < 2^n`.

D8.name: FRC.Reductio.decideAllSubsets
D8.doc: 5:D8 (Proposition finiteness, the finite direction): over a finite domain a second-order quantifier over all subsets is a finite conjunction — decided by exhaustive evaluation.

D8.name: FRC.Reductio.nat_embeds
D8.doc: 5:D8 (the infinite direction, its first step): an infinite domain carries a copy of `ℕ` — Dedekind's embedding, from which the reduction of true second-order arithmetic proceeds.

E1.name: FRC.Reductio.finite_choice
E1.doc: 5:E1 (Proposition finite-choice): on a finite universe with a canonical order, `ch(A) = min A` is a member of every nonempty `A` — choice is a definable theorem, not a postulate.

E1.name: FRC.Reductio.leastBelow_spec
E1.doc: 5:E1 (Proposition finite-choice) — the choice is a member, below the bound, and the least one.

E1.name: FRC.Reductio.leastBelow_some
E1.doc: 5:E1 — a nonempty family has a choice: if some `x < n` has `P x`, `leastBelow P n` is defined.

E2.name: FRC.Reductio.periodic_choice
E2.doc: 5:E2 (Lemma periodic-equality): for an equality-periodic family `A (i + N) = A i` the choice `min A i` is periodic with the same period.

E2.name: FRC.Reductio.leastBelow_congr
E2.doc: 5:E2 (Lemma periodic choice) — the choice depends on the set alone: pointwise equal families choose alike, so an equality-periodic family `A_{i+N} = A_i` has a choice function of the same period.

E3.name: FRC.Reductio.equivariant_section_iff
E3.doc: 5:E3 (Theorem equivariant-choice, one orbit): for a `G`-family `π : A → I` over a transitive `G`-set `I`, an equivariant section exists iff the stabiliser of a base point `i₀` fixes some point of its fibre.

E4.name: FRC.Reductio.obstruction_five
E4.doc: 5:E4 (Example basis-obstruction): on the line over `𝔽₅` the involution `v ↦ −v` fixes no basis — `−v ≠ v` for every `v ≠ 0` — while over `𝔽₂` it fixes `1`: the obstruction is arithmetic.

E4.name: FRC.Reductio.obstruction_five
E4.doc: 5:E4 (Example basis-obstruction) — on the line over `𝔽₅` the map `v ↦ −v` fixes no basis: `−v ≠ v` for every `v ≠ 0`; over `𝔽₂` it fixes `1`, so the obstruction is arithmetic.

E5.name: FRC.Reductio.repeat_below
E5.doc: 5:E5, 5:C5 (Lemma periodic König, the pigeonhole) — on `n` states the iteration from `x` revisits a state within `n` steps: some `i < j ≤ n` have `f^i x = f^j x`.

E5.name: FRC.Reductio.eventually_periodic
E5.doc: 5:E5 — the walk is eventually periodic: from step `i` on, period `p = j − i` with `0 < p ≤ n`, `f^(i+k+p) x = f^(i+k) x` for every `k`.

E8.name: FRC.Reductio.no_doubling
E8.doc: 5:E8 (Banach–Tarski disappears): a finite nonempty set cannot be doubled — there is no injection `X ⊕ X ↪ X`, so no decomposition reassembles two copies of `X` from pieces of `X`.

E8.name: FRC.Reductio.ultrafilter_principal
E8.doc: 5:E8 (ultrafilters): on a finite set every ultrafilter is principal.

V2.name: FRC.Reductio.stable
V2.doc: 5:B6 (Theorem stability, schema form) — every `Δ₀` formula takes its standard value in every frame `W_N` with `N > t(φ)`: `W_N ⊨ φ* ⟺ ℕ ⊨ φ`, for every environment, by induction on the formula.
